visual.caption: Deep fascia under the skin; the perineum is the commonest site (Fournier's in scrotum or vulva).

events.x: Pain out of proportion, erythema, swelling, fever

visuals.title: Do not wait for scans
nodes: Bloods: CRP, WCC up, metabolic acidosis
USS, CT or MRI: gas, fluid in fascia

visuals.title: How fascia is destroyed
nodes: Skin spared at first: exam lags

glossary.Deep fascia: Tough connective tissue sheet wrapping muscles, beneath the fat; infection spreads fast along it.
glossary.Subcutaneous tissue: The fatty layer between the skin and the deep fascia.
glossary.Immunosuppression: Weakened immune defences, from drugs or disease.
glossary.Pain out of proportion: Pain far worse than the skin appearance suggests: the hallmark warning of necrotising fasciitis.
glossary.Blistering: Formation of fluid-filled bubbles in the skin.
glossary.Gangrenous: Dead and decaying tissue, often black, from lost blood supply or infection.
glossary.Gangrene: Death of body tissue from loss of blood supply or infection.
glossary.Demarcated: Having a clear edge; poorly demarcated means the border fades out.
glossary.Amputation: Surgical removal of a limb or part of one.
glossary.Scrotum: The skin pouch holding the testes.
glossary.Perineum: The area between the genitals and the anus.
glossary.Ultrasound: Imaging with sound waves; fluid and air between fascial layers suggest deep infection.
glossary.Fascial layers: The sheets of fascia separating fat and muscle.
glossary.Fascial planes: Gaps between fascial layers that infection tracks along.
glossary.MRI: Magnetic resonance imaging: detailed soft tissue scans without radiation.
glossary.Imaging: Scans such as X-ray, ultrasound, CT or MRI.
glossary.Broad-spectrum: Antibiotics that cover many types of bacteria at once.
glossary.Empirically: Treating before the organism is known, based on the likely causes.
glossary.Critical care: Intensive care unit support for organ failure.
glossary.Thrombosis: Clot formation inside a blood vessel.
glossary.Ischaemia: Inadequate blood supply, starving tissue of oxygen.
glossary.Toxins: Poisonous substances made by bacteria that damage tissue.
glossary.Supportive care: Treatment that keeps the body going (fluids, oxygen, monitoring) while the cause is fixed.
glossary.Surgical debridement: Surgical cutting away of all dead and infected tissue.
